Full record in hand. Now I'll log the search and update the plan item status simultaneously.

## Search Results — pli_001: Wiltshire Baptism of Job Purnell

**Search executed:** `record_search` — surname: Purnell, given: Job, birth 1821–1831, England, record type: birth
**Collection hit:** England, Wiltshire, Church Records, 1518-1990 (coll. 4380174)
**Log entry:** log_001 | pli_001 → `in_progress`

---

### Candidate Found — ⚠️ Needs Review Before Extraction

| Field | Result |
|---|---|
| Name | Job Purnell |
| Event | Christening, **5 August 1821** |
| Place | Trowbridge, Wiltshire, England ✓ |
| Father | Samuel Purnall |
| Mother | Eliza Crabb |
| matchScore | 0.86 (matchConfidence 4) |
| Attached to subject | No |

**The conflict:** The baptism record is dated **1821**, but the tree carries Job's birth as *about 1826* — a **5-year discrepancy**. That is outside the 1–2 year tolerance where census rounding or indexing imprecision provides a ready explanation. A 5-year gap in a name-and-place match is the classic signature of a *same-named relative* (an uncle, older cousin, or earlier child of the same father), not proof the record belongs to our subject. I cannot report Samuel Purnall and Eliza Crabb as Job's parents on the strength of this match alone.

---

### What Would Settle It

The tree already holds a 1851 census source (S1). **The 1851 census age is the decisive anchor:**

- If the census recorded Job as **age 30** (born ~1821), the dates align — this baptism is almost certainly his, and extraction can proceed.
- If the census recorded Job as **age 25** (born ~1826), the dates do *not* align — this is a different Job Purnell, and we need to search the same Wiltshire church records for a second baptism in the 1824–1828 window.

**Proposed next step:** Run record-extraction on the 1851 census (S1) — or if the census was already extracted, check what age was recorded — to confirm whether the tree's "about 1826" estimate came from an age-25 or age-30 return. That single fact resolves the conflict without any new search.

## 1850 Census Search — Patrick Flynn, Schuylkill County (pli_001)

**Search:** `record_search` — surname "Flynn", givenName "Patrick", residence Schuylkill County PA, 1850, birth 1840–1850, United States Census

---

### Result — ⚠️ Needs Review

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | Patrick Flynn |
| Birth | 1845, Ireland |
| Residence (1850) | Branch Township, Schuylkill, Pennsylvania |
| Collection | United States Census, 1850 (FamilySearch coll. 1401638) |

| matchScore | **0.85** (matchConfidence 5/10) |
| Attached to subject? | No |
| Record role | **Head** |

---

### ⚠️ Why this is flagged needs-review

The record assigns this Patrick Flynn — birth date **1845**, Ireland — the role of **Head of household** in the 1850 census. A child born in 1845 would be approximately **5 years old** in 1850; a 5-year-old cannot be a head of household. This is a logical impossibility that overrides the 0.85 match score.

Two important caveats apply to pre-1880 census records:

- **No relationship column exists in the 1850 census.** "Head," "wife," "son" and similar designations are entirely **the indexer's inference** from listing order, age, sex, and surname — not anything stated in the original record.
- The full `record_read` returned **no co-residents** — no household members appear alongside Patrick in the indexed record. A genuine household headed by a 5-year-old alone is not a plausible finding.

This pattern suggests one of two things: **(a)** the indexed record is for a **child named Patrick Flynn** in a larger household, and FamilySearch has mistakenly labelled him "Head" because he was the first or only person on the indexed form, or **(b)** this is a **different, older Patrick Flynn** in Schuylkill County whose birth year was mis-transcribed as 1845.

---

### What would settle it

**Review the census image.** The image will show all persons enumerated in the same dwelling, their listed ages, and their sequence in the household. If the household head is actually Thomas Flynn (age ~32) with Patrick listed as a ~5-year-old child, this record almost certainly belongs to the subject — and would directly support the parentage question. If the head is Patrick himself at an adult age, this is a namesake.

The image ARK was not returned by `record_read` in this pass, so the next step is to locate the scan via the collection and page to the household. Alternatively, the **record-extraction** skill can be invoked once image review confirms the household structure — **not before**.
